newsitem.title: USA: GM strikes hit Q2 net by $490 million.
newsitem.headline: GM strikes hit Q2 net by $490 million.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday in a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing that strikes will bring down its second quarter income by $490 million or $0.67 a share on an after-tax basis.
The automaker said it has lost production of 96,000 units in the second quarter from the strikes at its Oklahoma City, Okla., passenger car plant and Pontiac, Mich., full-size pickup truck plant.
The Oklahoma City strike started April 4 and ended May 27. Bargainers are still trying to settle the Pontiac work stoppage, which began April 22.
GM said in the filing it is "likely" to recover some of the lost units through increased truck production in the future.

The $490 million consists of losses to date of $375 million from its North American Operations; $85 million from its Delphi Automotive Systems; and $30 million from the Delco Electronics unit of Hughes Electronics Corp.
GM had previously said the strikes had hurt its earnings by $225 million as of May 15.
